header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, BENCH AT SUKKUR
Cr. Misc. Application No. S – 388 of 2025
[Muhammad Nawaz Sahito v. The State and others]
brief for Mr. Achar Khan Gabole,
Respondents 4 to 9 & 12 : Mr. Nusrat Hussain Memon, Advocate
Respondents 1 to 3 : Mr. Gulzar Ahmed Malano, Assistant
body: Adnan Iqbal Chaudhry J.– By this application under section 561-A Cr.P.C., the Applicant seeks to set-aside order dated 11.06.2025 (impugned order) passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate Sobhodero @ Ranipur on charge-sheet submitted under section 173 Cr.P.C. in Criminal Summary Case No. 40/2025. The charge-sheet implicated Respondents 4 to 12 in Crime No. 07/2025 registered at P.S. Hingorja on the information of the Applicant, alleging offences punishable under sections 380, 457 and 215 PPC i.e. for theft in dwelling house, house-breaking by night, and taking gift to help recover stolen property. By the impugned order, the learned Magistrate observed that the I.O. had not conducted a fair and impartial investigation, opined that the FIR was false, disposed of the same in class ‘B’ while observing that the SHO of the concerned P.S. was at liberty to initiate proceedings against the Applicant/Informant under section 182 PPC.
2. Learned counsel for the Applicant acknowledges that it is settled law that a police report submitted under section 173 Cr.P.C. does not bind the Magistrate, who may or may not agree with the same.

However, it was submitted that even if the learned Magistrate did not agree with the positive report submitted by the I.O., he could at best have cancelled the case under class ‘C’ as there was no material before him to opine that the Falak Sher v. The State (PLD 1967 SC 425).

Cr. Misc. Appln. No.S-388 of 2025 Page 2 of 3 FIR was false; and furthermore, the suggestion to the SHO to initiate proceedings against the Applicant under section 182 PPC, was without lawful authority.

3. Learned counsel for the private Respondents and learned Assistant Prosecutor General submitted that though an order upon a police report submitted under section 173 Cr.P.C. was essentially an administrative function, nevertheless it is settled law that in doing so the Magistrate has to act judicially;
therefore, where it was apparent that the FIR was false, the learned Magistrate was competent to treated the case under class ‘B’.

4. Heard learned counsel. The FIR, which was lodged on 21.01.2025 to report an incident of 11.06.2024, was implausible to begin with. It was reported by the Applicant/Informant that while he and other inmates of the house were asleep at night, robbers broke into their house and decamped with Rs. 22 million, 6 tola gold ornaments and certain documents; however, the Informant party was able to track their footprints to the house of the Respondents Javed and Asif, who admitted the theft alongside the other Respondents; that the Informant party then paid the Respondents Rs. 1.5 lakhs to return the stolen articles, which were of course not returned.

5. When the I.O. submitted a charge-sheet against the private Respondents, the learned Magistrate noted that the delay of over 7 months in lodging the FIR was unexplained; there was murderous enmity between the parties over landed property, with a prior FIR by some of the Respondents against the Informant and his brothers for offence under section 322 PPC, and civil suits over said property against the Informant and his brothers; and that, numerous applications had also been made by both sides against each to the DIGP Sukkur and the SSP Khairpur; whereas, no recovery had been made from the private Respondents, and all witnesses produced by the Informant were his nephews. More significantly, it was noticed by the Magistrate that the Applicant had earlier filed Cr. Misc. Application No.4148/2024 under section 22-A/B Cr.P.C. for registering an FIR for the same incident, which application had been dismissed vide order dated 07.11.2024, and yet the SHO of P.S. Hingorja proceeded to lodge an FIR; and furthermore, the incident Bahadur v. The State (PLD 1985 SC 62).
Cr. Misc. Appln. No.S-388 of 2025 Page 3 of 3 narrated in that Cr. Misc. Application and the number of persons accused therein, was quite different from that in the subject FIR.

6. Therefore, the Magistrate’s opinion that the FIR was false and that the investigation was dishonest, was not mere speculation. It was based on documents accompanying the investigation report. In my view, the Magistrate would have acted injudiciously had he ignored those facts and simply disposed of the case under class ‘C’. Therefore, the submission that there was no material before the Magistrate to conclude that the FIR was false, is incorrect.

7. As regards the Applicant’s exposure to proceedings for the offence under section 182 PPC, it is correct that section 195(1)(a) Cr.P.C. bars a Court from taking cognizance of such offence except upon a complaint in writing of the public servant concerned or of some other public servant to whom he is subordinate. Therefore, as also observed by the Supreme Court in Ali Adnan Sheikha v. I.G. Police Sindh (2026 SCMR 77), a Magistrate has no authority to issue directions to initiate proceedings under section 182 PPC. Having said that, no such direction was given by the learned Magistrate in this case. His observation that the SHO “was at liberty” to take action under section 182 PPC, is not to be treated as a direction to do so. That remains the prerogative of the SHO or the officer to whom he is subordinate.

8. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned order dated 11.06.2025 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate Sobhodero @ Ranipur in Criminal Summary Case No.40/2025, does not warrant interference. The application is dismissed.
